steps.title: Prepare Environment and Equipment
steps.instruction: Set up the physical testing area and software to ensure consistency and proper tracking.

substeps.instruction: Open SMART 3.003 program on the desktop and ensure the camera is connected to the rear USB port.
Wear disposable gloves and a lab coat.
Turn off overhead fluorescent lights and turn on side peripheral lights with white bulbs.
Place the tank on a support so the bottom is 20-24" above the floor.
Wipe the inside surface of the tub above the water surface to remove proximal cues (marks, smudges, or irregularities).
Fill the tank with water to a depth of 2cm below the top of the tank.
Opacify the water using 25mL of white, non-toxic, powdered or liquid paint; stir to ensure transparency.

steps.title: Adjust Water Temperature
steps.instruction: Ensure the water temperature is exactly 21ºC.

substeps.instruction: Check and record the temperature on the data sheet.
If too cold: scoop out a tub full of water and replace with hot water.
If too hot: slowly add ice from the ice machine until 21ºC is reached, stirring throughout.

steps.title: Configure Platform Position
steps.instruction: Place the 6x6cm solid plastic non-slip platform at the fixed location designated in the configuration file based on the trial type.

substeps.instruction: For Test Trials: Set platform top 1cm below water level (non-visible).
For Visible Trials: Set platform top 1cm above water level with dark colored tape.
For Probe Trials: Remove the platform from the water entirely.

steps.title: Perform Software Calibration
steps.instruction: Calibrate the tracking software for the current session.

substeps.instruction: Click 'Configuration' -> 'Calibrate'.
Horizontal Calibration: Place calibration ruler on the platform surface; set bars at the inside edges of the black tape; set to 30 units.
Vertical Calibration: Repeat the process using 'Centimeters' under the Units field; set to 30 units.

steps.title: Set Up Computer Experiment
steps.instruction: Initialize the experiment parameters in the software.

substeps.instruction: Select 'New Experiment' and enter the session name (CODE) (e.g., MWM 9-25-13 Cohort 1 Day 1).
Set 'Image Source' to 'Microsoft Lifecam Studio' (480x640 resolution).
In 'Configuration', place the non-visible platform in the center and the ruler on top; align red and green bars to the inside edges of the red tape in cm and click 'accept'.
In 'Zones Definition', load the 'MWM Template 10-10-13' template.
In 'Detection Settings', set Brightness to 175, Contrast to 125, Threshold to 60, and Erosion to 1; select 'Center of Mass' for Track Settings and check 'Detection' for all arenas.
In 'Time Settings', select 'Pre-set time', set 'Latency Period' to zero, and set 'Acquisition period' (e.g., 1 minute).
Under 'Stop Conditions', select the parameter: 'After 1 visit(s) to: [Platform]' for acquisition/visible trials, or 'When STOP button is pressed or time expires' for probe trials.

steps.title: Manage Subjects and Scheduling
steps.instruction: Input animal data and organize the testing order.

substeps.instruction: Click 'Subjects' and edit 'Subject_01' or add new subjects using the green plus icon (include ID and gender).
Use the 'Scheduler' to verify the correct cohort, day, and trial number.
Ensure animals are tested in groups of 4, with one group completing testing before the next starts.

steps.title: Conduct Testing Trials
steps.instruction: Execute the water maze trials following specific handling and timing protocols.

substeps.instruction: Lower the mouse by the base of the tail into the water at the designated departure point (A, B, C, or D) as close to the edge as possible.
Follow departure point order: A and C are 40cm from platform; B is 50cm from platform. (Females Day 5 morning order: B, C, A, B).
For Reversal (2 days after first series): Platform in zone 2; use specific release points (Day 1: D, A, D, C, A; Day 2: D, C, A, D; Day 3: C, D, A, C; Day 4: A, D, C, A; Day 5: D).
Start data acquisition in the software; the timer starts when an object is detected.
Record latency to find the platform. If the animal fails to reach it within 90 seconds, guide it to the platform by the tail while in water and push it face forward onto the platform.
Ensure the mouse remains on the platform for 30 seconds using a stopwatch. If it jumps off, restart the 30s timer; if it jumps off twice, hold it by the tail facing away from the investigator.
Score 'floating' time (non-swimming) on a scale of 0-9 (0 = no floating; 1 = <10s; 2 = 11-20s, etc., up to 9 = full 90s). Use a stopwatch to sum all floating intervals.
Dry the mouse with a towel and place it in a clean, empty cage with a wire bar lid on a heating pad.

steps.title: Perform Probe Trial (Day 5)
steps.instruction: Assess spatial bias without the platform.

substeps.instruction: Verify water level is 1cm above where the platform would be, then remove the platform.
Set 'Stop Conditions' to 'When STOP button is pressed or time expires'.
Release the animal at the center of the zone opposite where the platform was located and allow it to swim freely for 90 seconds.

steps.title: Save and Export Data
steps.instruction: Process the recorded data into a final dataset.

substeps.instruction: Click 'Save' after each trial and name the file (e.g., PI Name MWM Cohort 1 Day 1).
In 'Analysis', drag trials to the center window and assign the 'MWM Template 10-10-13.SMZ' zone definition.

Under 'Report Definition' -> 'Summary Report', edit calculations to include Subject Info, Experimental Info, Trial Info, and specific Tracking Info (Distance in Zone %, Distance in Zone sec, Entries in Zone, Latency 1st entry, Resting Time %, Resting Time sec, Time in Zone %, Time in Zone sec, Total Distance, Dist. to Target, Latency to Target, and Mean Dist. to Target).
For Probe Trials, specifically include 'Target Crossing'.
Ensure 'Full Trial' is checked under Time Interval, click 'Analyze', then 'Export' to an Excel spreadsheet.
Manually insert columns H and I into the Excel file (between Trial Duration and Distance in Zone - Platform) to enter the float time (sec) and float score.
